provenance.how: constructed from the ADR's burst rule and the lane's ruling (the digest is a VISIBLE alert, not the silent attention form), and cross-checked against the core's own builder and key recipe (tests/unit/mobile/test_push_payload.py); not captured from a running relay, because no relay route emits the machine-side shapes yet

sound_values.default: the computer's `system` choice: the phone plays its OS default notification sound (iOS aps.sound = "default"; Android sound.default)
sound_values.none: notifications.sound.enabled is false on the computer: the banner posts silently (iOS omits aps.sound; Android uses the silent sound.none channel)
sound_values.fallback: soft-pulse — any computer selection that is not a built-in (a custom sound, or a hand-edited id that names nothing) sends soft-pulse in data.sound, because a phone that does not hold the custom file must still play the default rather than an OS sound; the custom file travels by name in the reserved, optional sound_custom (not sent yet)
sound_values.custom: c_<sha256[:16]> (lowercase hex; custom_pattern) — RESERVED, carried only by the optional sound_custom (not by sound), only when the selection is a custom sound and enabled is true; not sent yet

notes: A DIGEST IS NOT THE ATTENTION FORM. §3.2 fixes the attention form's envelope as a silent, best-effort wake (aps.content-available), so a coalesced catch-up riding it would arrive with no banner, no body and no count the user can read. type: "digest" is the signal the cloud's fan-out composes an ALERT from: a house constant plus the count, never a conversation name, a snippet or an error line.

No conversation, no completion_token and no kind: a digest spans conversations, so it names none of them, and a tap on it resolves nowhere — it is a "look at the app" nudge, and the app reads the truth from the machine.

COLLAPSE PER COMPUTER, not per conversation: the cloud derives apns-collapse-id / notification.tag as digest:<computer handle> from this payload's type and computer. A phone that already has banners queued for several conversations must not get one banner per conversation for a burst that is one event.
The machine sends no aps envelope (payload-forbidden-fields.json): the alert above is the text the cloud wraps, and aps.badge is never sent at all (§1.5).

alert is COMPOSED BY THE MACHINE and delivered verbatim (the lane's ruling, merged as §3.2 at digest_rules_ref): the title is APP_NAME, and the body's leading phrase is digest_subtitle's answer for the SET — "Complete" here because the batch is uniformly complete, "Mixed outcomes" when it is not — followed by the count. A fixed "Task complete" would announce a set of failures as complete, which is the claim the TUI's own digest vocabulary exists to refuse; a batch whose kinds could not be read makes NO claim at all and sends the count alone, because an empty subtitle is the house's own answer for a set it cannot characterise.
ONE NUMBER, ONE NOUN, AND THE NOUN AGREES WITH THE NUMBER: the count term is `<n> conversation(s) need(s) you`, so a count of one reads `1 conversation needs you`. alert_count_one files that literal.

THE WINDOW'S emit_id IS PERSISTED (digest_rules_ref §3.4): minted once when the coalescing window closes, reused on restart for that same window, and cleared on the same three exits the completion path uses — because a digest is the one VISIBLE type, so a re-minted key after a restart would show the user the same banner twice.

exclude is PERMITTED here with the attention form's meaning and is NEVER REQUIRED (§3.2 at digest_rules_ref): the required case belongs to the attention emit alone, because what makes it required is an ack, and the nudge an ack produces emits the per-conversation attention correction, never a catch-up digest. A digest that happens to follow an ack in time is not the same thing as one triggered by it. Absent means "exclude nobody", which is what the tick-detected path sends; exclude_absent_payload is a whole valid payload, not an empty list.

The key is sha256("digest" ‖ emit_id ‖ computer) — see emit-idempotency-keys.json, which carries the worked vector. The emit_id is minted ONCE when the coalescing window closes and is PERSISTED with the positions that window speaks for, so a restart mid-window re-emits the SAME key; re-minting per attempt would give one batch a new identity each time and defeat the cloud's dedupe (review round 1, B1; the persistence rule is digest_rules_ref §3.4).
count is §3.2's count: the machine's unread conversation count at composition time, the one aggregate the design discloses to the cloud on purpose.

sound is the computer's selected notification sound, MAPPED by the cloud and never composed from (notification-sounds design §3.6, ADR 0006 amendment), per value. iOS: a built-in id → aps.sound = "<id with - → _>.wav" (e.g. "soft_pulse.wav": the bundled file name, because Android res/raw names must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and expo-notifications applies one sounds: list to both platforms; data.sound itself still carries the catalog id); "default" → aps.sound = "default" (the OS default sound); "none" → aps.sound OMITTED (an unknown file name would make APNs play the default sound, the opposite of the setting). Android: android.channel_id = "sound.<id>" for a built-in, "sound.default" for default, and the silent "sound.none" channel for none (a channel's sound is fixed at creation). A custom selection, or any id the phone has no file for, sends soft-pulse (the phone may not hold the custom file; sound_custom, reserved below, names it for a device that does); notifications.sound.enabled false sends none. The computer's volume does not travel: the phone plays at its own notification volume. sound_values lists every value the field may carry.

sound_custom and devices[].sound_custom_ready are RESERVED, OPTIONAL and NOT SENT YET (ADR 0006 amendment 2026-11-04; notification-sounds addendum 2 §2.2): the phone will fetch the computer's custom sound through the tunnel and cache it, and the cloud picks PER DEVICE — sound_custom_ready true → iOS aps.sound = "<sound_custom>.wav", Android channel_id = "sound.<sound_custom>"; otherwise it maps data.sound exactly as above, which stays required and still carries soft-pulse for a custom selection. sound_custom is "c_<sha256[:16]>" of the stored WAV, lowercase hex, matching sound_values.custom_pattern ^c_[0-9a-f]{16}$ (the cloud validates the SHAPE, not only the type, because it splices the value into aps.sound and an Android channel id), never the user's sound name, so P2 holds; the underscore makes the wire value the phone's file stem (c_<sha16>.wav), so there is no second mapping. They are declared now because the cloud validates with extra="forbid": reserving them before S7 builds avoids a cloud-first deploy when core's notification-sounds C5 starts emitting them. reserved_not_sent lists them, and the suite asserts today's builder output carries neither.
